sampling_model.design: Population observational identification; there is no intervention or randomization design.
sampling_model.units: One scalar random vector indexed by the finite layered vertex set, with only \(X\) observed.
sampling_model.treatment: None; the target is the causal structure rather than a treatment effect.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None in the core theorem. The partial functional \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}\) is determined by the observed law on \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), and oracle evaluation cost is excluded from query complexity.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The full binary adjacency matrix is identifiable up to permutation of latent variables, using measured pure descendants as recursive surrogates in an exhaustive subset construction.
The proposed algorithm can find the correct Markov equivalence class of the whole graph asymptotically under proper restrictions.
The estimated variable and the true variable are equivalent up to an invertible transformation.
Trek separation gives a complete characterization of when covariance submatrices drop rank and their generic lower rank.

body.tldr: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang already identify the full binary adjacency matrix of their nonlinear latent hierarchy and already reuse measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates. The contribution is a deterministic RankPeel protocol that replaces their exhaustive subset construction by pairwise pure-block tests and representative-neutrality deletion, giving at most \(p^2+p\) observed queries and \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping on complete runs. To keep those queries invariant under the observed law, the rank functional is defined only where all continuously differentiable conditional-mean representatives have the same essential-supremum derivative rank; RankPeel returns \(\bot\) otherwise. Exact recovery on complete runs, the restricted separator and private-path lemmas, and the quadratic bound are theorem targets. Whether the unchanged published Conditions 1--3 guarantee version stability and hence completeness for every class member is the explicit analytic open question; replay is only a corollary.

project_justification.gap: The closest nonlinear result already identifies the complete binary adjacency matrix and already uses measured pure descendants as recursive surrogates, but its construction exhaustively searches subset families and gives no explicit polynomial bound on observed rank queries. Its pointwise conditional-mean derivative notation also does not establish invariance across regular-conditional versions.
project_justification.niche: The same published model class admits a potentially sharper algorithmic formulation: pairwise block discovery and monotone parent deletion can reduce the number of observed-law rank decisions, provided every adaptive derivative-rank query is version-stable.
project_justification.fill: RankPeel supplies the deterministic pairwise and deletion protocol, a \(p^2+p\) complete-run query bound, and a replay corollary. A law-invariant stability domain prevents arbitrary pointwise versions from entering the oracle, while the exact Conditions 1--3 completeness obligation remains an open theorem-level boundary rather than a new assumption.

body.related_work: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang identify the full binary adjacency matrix up to latent permutation and use measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates; Theorem 2 tightens only the query construction, replacing their exhaustive subset search by a deterministic pairwise and deletion protocol with an explicit quadratic observed-query bound on version-stable complete runs. Huang, Low, Xie, Glymour, and Zhang inform the same pure-descendant surrogate motif in a linear IL\(^{2}\)H model, but their covariance-rank assumptions and Markov-equivalence target differ. Kong, Huang, Xie, Xing, Chi, and Zhang inform the layerwise nonlinear setting but identify latent representations through invertible transformations rather than an observed-law derivative-rank protocol. Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma inform the separation of graph-forced upper bounds from generic path-based lower bounds in linear Gaussian models. Chen and Fang and Cattaneo, Feng, and Shigida address the distinct nonregular rank-testing and uniform derivative-inference problems outside this population core.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The prescribed enumeration covered all \(676\) stated three-level graphs and all \(58{,}188\) proposed level-zero and retained-surrogate cuts, but finite enumeration does not prove the recursive graphical lemma. More importantly, the unchanged published Conditions 1--3 provide differentiable conditional-mean versions but do not by themselves identify a pointwise derivative rank across versions on arbitrary observed supports. The core therefore uses the observed-law domain \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), makes exact reconstruction conditional on a complete run, and leaves full-class version stability plus the restricted separator upper bound as the analytic obligation. No blanket separator-equals-rank identity, saturated-rank condition, or faithfulness inheritance after latent contraction is assumed.
body.honest_scope: The target remains population recovery of the full binary adjacency matrix on the unchanged Prashant--Ng--Zhang--Huang class, not a stronger identified graph than the anchor provides. The settled proposal-level advance sought is algorithmic: deterministic pairwise and deletion queries, a quadratic complete-run bound, and a replay corollary. Exact recovery is stated only when every adaptive pair lies in the observed-law version-stability domain. Whether the published Conditions 1--3 force that completeness and the restricted separator upper bound is open. The proposal does not cover polynomial-time evaluation of the oracle, nonparametric Jacobian estimation, finite-sample recovery, or image-data consistency. In the nonsingular linear Gaussian special case, version stability holds and query ranks reduce to covariance-rank geometry.
